method.modelFamily: Audio Spectrogram Transformer fine-tuned on AudioSet
method.input: mono normalized waveform resampled from 44.1 kHz to 16 kHz
method.coarseWindows: contiguous 8-second windows from 0 to 56 seconds, 7.7 seconds from 56 to 63.7, then three bounded tail windows
method.followup: 2-second windows from 14 to 24 seconds to localize the coarse 16–24-second Ding result
method.amplitudeCrossCheck: ffmpeg silencedetect at -45 dB for >=0.5 seconds

acceptedObservations.observation: Music is a top-two semantic label in every bounded coarse window, supporting a recurrent background-music bed beneath narration.
A ding-like sound is localized to the 22–24-second followup window; it functions as a brief transition/emphasis accent around the model-specification change.
Tail is silence-dominant; semantic windows agree with the amplitude detector's silence boundary.

rejectedOrUnresolvedLabels: Camera/gunshot/cap-gun labels in 32–40 seconds are low or unstable and are not accepted as literal source events.
Chopping/chop labels in 40–56 seconds may reflect percussive/transient texture and are not accepted as literal food-chopping events.
The model's low residual Music probabilities in the amplitude-silent tail are not treated as audible music because Silence dominates and the independent amplitude detector reports continuous silence.
Exact music genre, track identity, ownership, mix level, and source are not established.
Exact production source of the 22–24-second ding-like sound is not established.
limitations: This is machine semantic listening, not human auditory review.
AudioSet class probabilities are proposals, not ground truth; only stable, repeated, time-localized observations are accepted.
The classifier evaluates mixed narration and non-speech audio rather than isolated stems.
No external copyright or track-identification service was used.
